\multicolumn{5}{@{}l}{\textit{Prey growth ($T_1$)}}\\[2pt]
G1 & $r>0$ & D & Intrinsic growth rate: the prey increases at low density without predators \cite{verhulst1838,lotka1925}. & -- \\
G2 & $K>0$ & D & Carrying capacity \cite{verhulst1838}. & -- \\
G3 & $\theta>0$; $\theta=1$ is the logistic law & D, M & Shape exponent of density dependence \cite{gilpin1973}. & \checkmark\ S1 \\
G4 & $\tau^{x}\ge 0$ & D & Delay in self-limitation \cite{hutchinson1948}. & -- \\
G5 & Without predators, $K$ is stable iff $r\tau^{x}<\pi/2$ & M & Roots of $\lambda+re^{-\lambda\tau}=0$ first cross the imaginary axis at $\lambda=ir$, $r\tau=\pi/2$, with $\mathrm{Re}\,d\lambda/d\tau=r^{2}/(1+\pi^{2}/4)>0$ \cite{hutchinson1948}. & \checkmark\ S6 \\
G6 & Gompertz: per-capita rate $r\ln(K/x)\to\infty$ as $x\to0^{+}$ & M & \cite{gompertz1825}. & \checkmark\ S7 \\
G7 & Strong Allee: $0<A<K$ & M & Per-capita growth $g(x)=r(1-x/K)(x-A)/K$ has $g(0)=-rA/K$ and zeros $A,K$ \cite{allee1931,wang2011allee}. & \checkmark\ S2a, S2c \\
G8 & Weak Allee: $-K<A\le 0$; $A\le -K$ removes the effect & M, C & $g'(0)=r(K+A)/K^{2}$. The borderline $A=0$ ($g(0)=0$) is grouped with the weak case by convention. & \checkmark\ S2b, S2d \\
G9 & Strong Allee, prey alone: origin locally stable, outcome depends on initial densities & M & Follows from $g(0)<0$ (statement corrected to ``without predators\textquotedblright{}). & \checkmark\ S2a \\
G10 & Additive Allee: strong iff $\mu>rb$; weak iff $rb^{2}/K<\mu<rb$ (needs $b<K$) & M & $g(0)=r-\mu/b$, $g'(0)=-r/K+\mu/b^{2}$; additive form from \cite{dennis1989}. & \checkmark\ S3a, S3b, S3c \\
G11 & Fear: $r>d$ & M & Low-density growth rate of the prey alone is $r-d$; model of \cite{wang2016fear} (abstract: cost of fear in prey reproduction). & \checkmark\ S4 \\
G12 & $d\ge 0$, $c^{x}>0$, $k\ge 0$ ($k=0$: no fear) & D & Death rate, self-limitation and fear level \cite{wang2016fear}. & -- \\
G13 & Fear lowers prey births only; the predator gains nothing from it & D, L & Model structure \cite{wang2016fear}. Field evidence: perceived risk alone cut offspring production by 40\% \cite{zanette2011} (abstract). & -- \\
G14 & $0\le\varepsilon<1$; $\omega=2\pi/T>0$ & M & $\min_{t} r(1+\varepsilon\sin\omega t)=r(1-\varepsilon)>0$ iff $\varepsilon<1$. & \checkmark\ S5 \\
G15 & Seasonal forcing: periodic solutions, multiple attractors and chaos instead of equilibria & D, L & Non-autonomous by construction. Periodic solutions \cite{cushing1977}; multiple attractors and chaos \cite{rinaldi1993}. Checked against the titles only (the open copy of \cite{rinaldi1993} is no longer online); ``quasi-periodic\textquotedblright{} was removed from the note. & -- \\
G16 & $\alpha_{ii'}\ge 0$ & D & Interspecific competition between prey. & -- \\

\multicolumn{5}{@{}l}{\textit{Predation ($T_2$)}}\\[2pt]
P1 & $a>0$ & D & Attack rate (search efficiency) \cite{holling1959}. & -- \\
P2 & $h>0$; maximal intake $1/h$ & M & $\lim_{x\to\infty} ax/(1+ahx)=1/h$ \cite{holling1959}. & \checkmark\ S9 \\
P3 & One handling time shared by all food items: $D_j=1+\sum_k a_kh_kx_k$ & M & Time budget $T=T_s\bigl(1+\sum_k a_kh_kx_k\bigr)$ gives intake $a_ix_i/D_j$; applies to prey, predator food and additional food alike. & \checkmark\ S12 \\
P4 & $G>0$; response peaks at $\sqrt{G}$, $\sqrt{G}/(1-\phi)$ or $\xi+\sqrt{G}$ & M & Holling IV / group defence \cite{andrews1968,freedman1986}. The builder stated $\sqrt{G}$ for every case; corrected for the two refuge types. & \checkmark\ S10a, S10b, S10c \\
P5 & Holling IV: at most two interior equilibria; Bogdanov--Takens bifurcations & M, L & Equilibria solve a quadratic. Bogdanov--Takens: \cite{xiao2001siam} (abstract); source added. & \checkmark\ S10d \\
P6 & Ivlev: $\rho,\lambda>0$ & D & \cite{ivlev1961}. & -- \\
P7 & Beddington--DeAngelis, Crowley--Martin: $c\ge 0$, $c=0$ is Holling II & M & \cite{beddington1975,deangelis1975,crowley1989}. & \checkmark\ S11a \\
P8 & Hassell--Varley: $0<\gamma<1$ & M, C & $\gamma=0$ gives Holling II and $\gamma=1$ the ratio-dependent form; the interval between them is a convention \cite{hassell1969}. & \checkmark\ S11b \\
P9 & Mutual interference: $0\le\nu<1$ & M & $\nu<1$ makes predation vanish without predators; $\nu=0$ is the classical term \cite{hassell1971}. & \checkmark\ S11c \\
P10 & Ratio dependence: not defined at $(0,0)$; origin can attract all orbits & M, L & 0/0 and direction-dependent derivative at the origin. Higher-order singular point with parabolic, elliptic and hyperbolic sectors \cite{xiao2001rd} (abstract); global stability conditions for each of the three equilibria, the origin included \cite{kuang1998} (abstract). ``Blow-up techniques\textquotedblright{} removed: not in either abstract. & \checkmark\ S28 \\
P11 & Herd behaviour: $0<p<1$; $p=1/2$ for a planar herd & M & The edge of a disc-shaped herd scales as area$^{1/2}$ \cite{ajraldi2011}. & \checkmark\ S8c \\
P12 & Herd: $x^{p}$ not Lipschitz at 0; prey can vanish in finite time & M & $\frac{d}{dt}x^{1-p}\to-(1-p)ay<0$ as $x\to0$ \cite{ajraldi2011}. & \checkmark\ S8a, S8b \\
P13 & $0\le\phi<1$; $\xi\ge 0$ & D & Protected fraction or number of prey \cite{maynardsmith1974,gonzalez2003}. & -- \\
P14 & Fixed-number refuge stabilises the Lotka--Volterra centre; a proportional refuge does not & M, L & Proportional refuge only rescales $a$ and keeps the first integral; fixed number gives trace $-r\xi/(x^{*}-\xi)<0$. Attributed to \cite{maynardsmith1974} (book, not accessed; result re-derived). Caveat from \cite{mcnair1986} (abstract): refuges can destabilise in more realistic models. The earlier note (``stabilises more strongly\textquotedblright{}) was replaced; source added. & \checkmark\ S29a, S29b \\
P15 & $0\le\kappa<1$ & D & Fraction of search efficiency lost to habitat complexity \cite{bairagi2011} (not accessed; publisher page behind a CAPTCHA). & -- \\
P16 & $w\ge 0$; cooperation gives a component Allee effect & M & Per-capita gain $e(a+wy)x/(1+(a+wy)hx)$ increases with $y$. & \checkmark\ S17 \\
P17 & Hunting cooperation can produce demographic Allee effects and predator collapse & L & \cite{teixeiraalves2017} (abstract). Earlier wording (``bistability\textquotedblright{}) replaced by the abstract's statement. & -- \\
P18 & Additional food: $\Lambda\ge 0$ constant; $a^{F},h^{F},e^{F}>0$; enters $D$ and $T_3$ & D, M & \cite{srinivasu2007} (abstract: handling times decide the outcome). Under Leslie--Gower only $a^{F},h^{F}$ appear (no conversion term). & \checkmark\ S12 \\

H1 & $q,E,H\ge 0$; $\ell$ constants $>0$ & D & \cite{clark1976,brauer1979,gupta2013,chaudhuri1996}. & -- \\

F1 & $D^{x},D^{y}>0$; no-flux boundary conditions & D & \cite{skellam1951}. & -- \\

K1 & Lotka--Volterra: centre at $(m/ea,\,r/a)$, first integral $H$ & M & \cite{lotka1925,volterra1926}. & \checkmark\ S23 \\
